notes: Stored edit (very_unlikely): the authorship is stated everywhere and follows from nothing. Kept from the scouting with the review's fixes: the prime query is worded 'traditionally credited with the first known proof', since the Elements compiles earlier work and who first proved it is unknown (R1). Background-belief queries: the 'father of geometry' epithet and the credit for the infinitude of primes can be stored under Euclid's name or through the work; the two storage choices are independent, so the record has 4 worlds. Risk considered: Wikipedia ties the epithet to the work ('chiefly known for the Elements'), which makes w2 likelier, but a model can keep Euclid as 'father of geometry' without having written this one book, so w1 is not dropped (README Decisions 4: lopsided worlds stay). The 'father of geometry' and 'Euclid's theorem' facts are listed as bridges of the per-world chains so the audit checks them. R1: Thales is occasionally called father of geometry (rare against Euclid). The edit is anachronistic (Archimedes was born after c. 300 BC), so no query asks dates. Prompts never say 'Euclid's Elements' (R2), and say 'thirteen books' to keep the work apart from chemical elements. Unlike most mathematics records this one has worlds: it edits a fact of the history of mathematics, which is contingent. The second derived query's original answer (no) rests on Euclid not having formulated the law of buoyancy, which is listed as a bridge with its own check.
